_note: Inputs to scripts/33_record_adapted_hermite.py.  Every number here is printed by scripts/32_adapted_hermite.py (--mode span | chaos | ceiling) or scripts/28_learned_corrector.py --mode score/--mode ship; this file exists so the ledger row and docs/hermite_rank_ceiling.md quote the same bytes.

span.frame: mean-field path matrix W^1 diag(Phi(a^1)) ... W^32, top 24 left singular vectors
span.notes: scripts/32 --mode span, 4 local MLPs (900000..900003) x 240,000 samples, 2,494 features in one design whose Gram is ANALYTIC (Mehler) -- coordinate layer-1 pure powers to degree 8, an orthonormal mean-field frame of 24 directions with all products to total degree 4 and pure powers to degree 16, and every cross term.  Coefficients fitted on one half, explained variance read on the other against the analytic Gram, so R2_pop is unbiased for the population span (the N -> inf limit) and carries no p/N inflation.  Degrees 3-8 of the coordinate family are worth 1.9 points in total; going from degree 2 to degree 16 on the adapted frame moves every row by under 0.02 points.  The argmax of eff R2 = R2_pop - 2p/8500 over all 71 dictionaries is the SHIPPED coord d<=2 basis.

chaos.notes: scripts/32 --mode chaos.  The OU/Mehler semigroup multiplies the degree-d chaos by t^d, so with x_t = t x + sqrt(1-t^2) xi the correlation C(t) = sum_j Cov(y_j(x), y_j(x_t)) / sum_j Var(y_j) equals sum_{d>=1} f_d t^d.  This is the Hermite DEGREE decomposition, not the coordinate-subset ANOVA decomposition of docs/floor_theorem.md -- He_2(x_1) has ANOVA order 1 and degree 2, so d_M = 11.5 was never the mean degree.  Cost is one extra forward pass per coupling and the variance is O(Var(y)^2/N): no curse of dimensionality.  f_1 = 26.7% reproduces the f_1 = 0.276 +- 0.016 of docs/floor_theorem.md from a seventh independent estimator, so the instrument validates itself.  C(1) = 1 identically gives the assumption-free bound sum_{d<=D} f_d <= min_t C(t)/t^D; the f_d are the NNLS inversion of the same C(t), an ill-posed Hausdorff moment problem, quoted as a smooth readout and not as a hard bound.

ceiling.notes: scripts/32 --mode ceiling.  Two exact bounds.  (1) The closed span of {prod_r He_{d_r}(<a_r,x>)} over all degrees and all products is exactly L^2(sigma(A^T x)), so R^2 <= sum_j Var(E[y_j | A^T x]) / sum_j Var(y_j) with no truncation in degree anywhere; measured by equiprobable binning with per-bin means from independent halves (unbiased).  For the top mean-field direction that ceiling is 19.77% and Hermite degrees 1 and 2 alone already give 19.87% -- degrees 3 through infinity along any single direction are worth zero.  (2) h_d(<a,x>) = sum_{|alpha|=d} sqrt(d!/alpha!) a^alpha H_alpha is exactly the unit RANK-ONE tensor a^(x)d, so an m-dimensional direction set spans Sym^2(A) at degree 2 and reaches at most sum_{k<=m} lambda_k(P) / tr(P) of f_2, with P = sum_j S_j^2 and S_j = E[ybar_j (x x^T - I)].  The bound is tight against the span surface (<=6.2 / <=3.6 / <=2.0 degree-2 points at m=16/8/4, measured 4.3 / 2.4 / 1.2).  The 256 layer-1 coordinate directions are the network's only FIXED kink normals and reach 73% of f_2 with 256 features; matching that with a shared-direction tensor basis needs m ~ 56, i.e. ~1,600 features.

ship.estimator: sparse MC (tau=2.5, N=8500, P=150) + layer-1 Hermite CVs k<=2 + 15-column offline ridge head -- UNCHANGED by round 9

Round 9 changed no shipped byte: the R^2(p,d) surface's argmax IS the shipped basis.
